key_insight: Hyperspectral imaging can separate donor and acceptor signals in real time, enabling inline quality mapping of roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical metrology route for scalable organic solar cell manufacturing, where continuous monitoring is needed to detect coating non-uniformity and material distribution issues.
method: Inline hyperspectral camera on a roll-to-roll slot-die coating setup
Multivariate curve resolution to resolve P3HT donor and OIDTBR acceptor spatial distributions
Spectral fitting of P3HT absorbance to estimate exciton bandwidth and aggregation state
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reliable spatial resolution of donor and acceptor contributions plus exciton-bandwidth mapping from measured absorbance spectra in coated active layers.
watch_item: Implementation will depend on robust calibration and spectral deconvolution under fast-moving, variable manufacturing conditions.
paper_title: Hyperspectral imaging for inline quality monitoring of roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers
